entities.name: Metformin
entities.coverageLabel: Partial evidence guide: Long COVID, plus selected local-corpus findings

overview.paragraph: Metformin is a medicine used for type 2 diabetes. Repurposing research asks whether it can change outcomes beyond glucose control: the recorded trials address later Long COVID after acute infection, recovery from established symptoms, and Parkinson disease. The results differ by question: COVID-OUT’s reported lower diagnosis hazard is provisional pending correction review, ACTIV-6 did not meet its primary efficacy threshold, and the recorded treatment and Parkinson comparisons did not demonstrate clinical benefit. The schizophrenia report is exploratory, while the sarcopenia material is a review rather than independently acquired trial evidence. These findings do not establish an overall benefit across diseases, and safety, interactions and current approved uses still need separate assessment.

entities.name: Nirmatrelvir with ritonavir
entities.coverageLabel: Partial evidence guide: established Long COVID regimens

overview.paragraph: Nirmatrelvir with ritonavir appears in the acquired textbook as a COVID-19 regimen; the chapter distinguishes nirmatrelvir from the older ritonavir component. The Long COVID trials assessed the combination after persistent symptoms were already present, with placebo plus ritonavir as the comparison. STOP-PASC did not show a significant primary symptom-severity benefit, and the RECOVER-VITAL abstract reports no significant primary benefit across its selected phenotypes. The fatigue confidence interval in STOP-PASC includes differences in either direction, so an exact zero effect has not been established. This evidence concerns the tested combination and durations; it does not answer whether unboosted nirmatrelvir works or provide current approval, interaction or prescribing guidance.

entities.name: Itraconazole
entities.coverageLabel: Background overview: cancer efficacy synthesis pending original reports

overview.paragraph: Itraconazole is described in the acquired textbook as an antifungal medicine used for systemic fungal infections. Its cancer-repurposing rationale in that chapter concerns cell-signalling pathways discussed for colon cancer, pancreatic cancer and melanoma. The bibliography also identifies reports of itraconazole combined with chemotherapy in recurrent or persistent ovarian clear cell carcinoma and metastatic pancreatic cancer. Those are specific research leads: neither their titles nor a textbook summary establish a benefit across cancers or reveal the size and uncertainty of a treatment effect. The original reports are still pending acquisition, so this overview cannot judge anticancer efficacy, treatment safety or interactions, and it is not a completed cancer evidence guide.

conditions.name: Long COVID
conditions.coverageLabel: Partial evidence guide: selected metformin and nirmatrelvir–ritonavir trials

overview.paragraph: The treatment trials use Long COVID or postacute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection for persistent problems after infection, but they enroll different symptom groups and measure different outcomes. A central distinction is timing: metformin prevention trials start during acute COVID, whereas the metformin and nirmatrelvir–ritonavir treatment trials start after persistent symptoms are established. The recorded prevention findings are outcome-dependent, while the treatment comparisons summarized here did not demonstrate their expected primary benefit. These results do not define every Long COVID phenotype or settle every proposed treatment; full-text gaps, a quarantined report and unfinished appraisal remain visible alongside the estimates.

synthesisRows.use: Computational drug-repurposing hypothesis for anti-TNF-refractory Crohn disease
synthesisRows.population: GSE100833 anti-TNF refractory Crohn's disease inflamed and non-inflamed colonic transcriptomes; CMap and STRING analyses.
synthesisRows.comparison: Transcriptomic cluster queried against Connectivity Map drug profiles; no treated-patient comparison
synthesisRows.endpoint: Connectivity Map (CMap) enrichment score for a selected gene cluster
synthesisRows.timepoint: Computational analysis; no patient treatment follow-up
synthesisRows.route: Not applicable: no drug administered to patients

finding.text: Clomipramine was nominated by an original computational analysis of Crohn disease transcriptomes. The result identifies a hypothesis for experimental testing and does not demonstrate symptom improvement, remission or clinical safety.

synthesisRows.magnitudeText: CMap enrichment score 8.4, cluster 2. This is a computational score, not a clinical effect size; a clinical effect interval is not identifiable from this design.
synthesisRows.evidenceBase: One original computational analysis; the source describes transcriptomes from 327 patients, with no new intervention cohort. Both Crohn candidate rows belong to this same analysis.
synthesisRows.studyFamilyIdentityState: One report-based computational analysis; both nominated drugs share this family. Broader duplication reconciliation pending.

limitations.text: The analysis used one transcriptome dataset; the authors note potential selection bias and the need for experimental confirmation.
Candidate nomination cannot quantify patient benefit, and neither drug was tested as a Crohn treatment in this report.

synthesisRows.population: Active vitiligo, as summarized in a textbook

finding.text: The textbook summarizes a randomized trial as finding no added benefit from atorvastatin for repigmentation or halting vitiligo progression when added to narrowband UVB. The original trial report is not part of the acquired primary corpus.

synthesisRows.magnitudeText: No numerical treatment effect or confidence interval is recorded. The book describes 30 participants; that sample count is not an effect size.
synthesisRows.evidenceBase: One textbook summary of a bicentric, prospective, randomized, single-blind trial. Zero independently acquired original studies in this row.

limitations.text: The summary cannot replace the original report for endpoint definitions, analysis, harms or uncertainty.
This background null finding is retained without implying that it settles every atorvastatin formulation or vitiligo regimen.
